newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Datacraft wins US$220,000 Taiwan deal.
newsitem.headline: Datacraft wins US$220,000 Taiwan deal.

text.p: Datacraft Asia Ltd, a communications and network systems integrator, said on Monday it had won a US$220,000 installation contract from China Airlines of Taiwan.
The contract involved the installation of Cisco System's channel interface processor for high-speed direct connection to the airlines' existing IBM mainframes.
Datacraft said in a statement the CIP was a high-performance interface processor that gave IBM and IBM-compatible mainframes faster networking access by connecting directly to the mainframe channel.
It said Cisco CIP was cost-effective as users were no longer required to pay for the high software, licence and maintenance fees required for every IBM front end processor.
The company said the contract paved the way for Datacraft to penetrate the lucrative market of mainframe communications processors hitherto restricted largely to IBM.
